before.title: 3.3T Oil Consumption with Smoke and Fouled Plugs
before.description: Some 3.3T owners report elevated engine-oil consumption — in one documented case roughly 2 quarts over a ~320-mile trip, accompanied by bluish exhaust smoke indicating oil burning. The consumed oil contributes to heavy intake-valve carbon (the 3.3T is direct-injected), sooty/wet spark plugs, and multi-cylinder misfire codes. Consumption is intermittent across the fleet (many cars use little to no oil), so owners should monitor levels between changes rather than assume the engine is unaffected.
before.solution: Document consumption with a dealer oil-consumption test (measured top-offs over a set mileage) while the powertrain warranty is in force. Inspect the PCV system and turbo seals for oil ingestion, replace fouled spark plugs, and clean carboned intake valves (walnut blast) if buildup is found. Check the oil level frequently between changes and use the correct spec oil; severe consumption may require dealer powertrain repair under warranty.
symptoms: Oil level dropping noticeably between changes
Bluish/grey exhaust smoke, especially on startup or under load
Low-oil warning earlier than expected
Fouled (sooty/wet) spark plugs and misfire codes
Heavy intake-valve carbon found at service

before.title: ABS Module Electrical Short Causing Engine-Bay Fire Risk (Recall 21V-161 / 007G)
before.description: An electrical short circuit can develop inside the Anti-lock Brake System (ABS) hydraulic control module. Because the module is always powered, the short can cause an engine-compartment fire whether the vehicle is parked or being driven, even with the ignition off. Genesis recalled certain 2019-2021 G70 vehicles under NHTSA campaign 21V-161 (Genesis recall 007G); owners were told to park the car outside and away from structures until repaired. This is part of the broader Hyundai/Genesis ABS-fire recall family. The remedy installs a fuse in the ABS module wiring to prevent the short from igniting a fire.
before.solution: Confirm the VIN against Recall 21V-161 (007G) and have the free remedy performed — dealers add a multi-fuse to the ABS module's power supply so a short can't start a fire. Until repaired, park outdoors away from buildings. If the ABS warning light is on or the module has already been damaged, the hydraulic electronic control unit (HECU/ABS module) is inspected and replaced as needed.
symptoms: Burning or melting-plastic smell from the engine bay
ABS / brake / traction-control warning lights illuminated
Smoke from under the hood while parked or driving
Blown fuses related to the ABS circuit

before.title: Electronic Parking Brake (EPB) Actuator Failure — Won't Release or Engage
before.description: The rear electronic parking brake actuator (rear caliper motor) can fail electrically or mechanically, leaving the EPB stuck engaged (car won't move) or refusing to set. Owners report a persistent 'Push EPB Switch' warning with a blinking EPB indicator, sometimes surfacing when the Auto Hold feature malfunctions at a stop. Because the actuator is integrated into the rear caliper assembly, dealers often replace the actuator/caliper and recalibrate rather than servicing a sub-component. Diagnostic tip from owners: press the EPB switch and listen — motor noise points to a single failed actuator, while total silence points to a switch or controller fault. This is an electromechanical actuator/control fault, distinct from any front friction-surface (rotor) issue.
before.solution: Diagnose for EPB actuator/control-module fault codes and check for a stuck Auto Hold condition. Accepted fix is replacement of the rear EPB actuator (typically as part of the rear caliper assembly) followed by system calibration/clearing via a scan tool. Some owners have reset a stuck system temporarily by pulling the relevant fuses with the engine running, but replacement is the durable fix; some cases resolved under warranty goodwill.
symptoms: 'Push EPB Switch' dashboard message
Blinking/flashing EPB warning light
Parking brake will not release, car won't move
Parking brake will not engage
Auto Hold engages brake and won't let go at a stop

before.title: Front Brake Rotor Warping / Pulsation (Brembo Pad Deposit and Early Warping)
before.description: G70 owners frequently report a steering-wheel and brake-pedal pulsation that feels like warped rotors, sometimes appearing at very low mileage (reports as early as ~7,000-11,000 miles) and even all four rotors at once. On Brembo-equipped cars the cause is often uneven friction-material transfer (pad deposits) baking onto the rotor surface rather than true thickness variation — the factory ceramic-style pads don't always reach enough temperature to scrub off deposits. Some cars do show genuine early rotor distortion. Genesis has acknowledged the Brembo brake vibration concern, and the same complaint is widely documented on the platform-mate Kia Stinger.
before.solution: First try a proper bedding-in procedure (a series of firm high-speed stops) to even out and burn off pad deposits — this resolves the pulsation for many owners. If pulsation persists, measure rotor thickness variation/runout; machine or replace warped rotors and fit pads that run hotter/cleaner. Many owners upgrade to aftermarket slotted rotors and more aggressive pads. OEM front rotor for Brembo cars is 51712-J5500; DBA 4000-series slotted rotors are a common direct-fit upgrade.
symptoms: Steering-wheel shimmy or shudder when braking from highway speed
Pulsating brake pedal
Vibration felt in the seat under braking
Symptom returns a few thousand miles after rotor service

before.title: GDI Intake-Valve Carbon Buildup (Misfires, Rough Idle)
before.description: Like most gasoline direct-injection engines without supplemental port injection, the G70's 2.0T and 3.3T accumulate carbon on the backs of the intake valves over time because no fuel washes them. Owners report heavy valve coking by ~24,000 miles in some cases, especially when combined with oil consumption. The deposits disrupt airflow and seating, causing rough idle, hesitation, cold-start stumble, and cylinder misfire codes. Removing the intake to walnut-blast the valves is the definitive fix.
before.solution: Definitive repair is mechanical intake-valve cleaning (walnut-blasting / media blasting) after removing the intake manifold — typically due around 40,000-80,000 miles depending on driving and oil use. Address any contributing oil consumption (PCV/valve guides) at the same time. A quality top-tier fuel, regular oil changes, and an occasional Italian tune-up slow accumulation; catch-can installation reduces future buildup. Replace fouled spark plugs and clear misfire codes after cleaning.
symptoms: Rough or uneven idle, especially cold
Hesitation / stumble at low speed
Cylinder misfire codes, sometimes a check engine light
Reduced fuel economy and power
Hard / rough cold start

before.title: Headlight Condensation and Moisture Causing Lighting Failure
before.description: Moisture inside the headlamp assembly is one of the most widely reported G70 complaints across all model years. The vented housings draw in humid air, and when the internal seal or desiccant fails, water streaks, large droplets, or pooling collect in the housing. Persistent water intrusion can short the internal LED/turn-signal electronics, in some cases killing the blinker and requiring full assembly replacement. Genesis issued a TSB stating light fogging that clears within a few minutes is normal, but visible water streaks, large droplets, or pooling indicate a failed seal that warrants replacement. Note the 2019-2021 (pre-facelift) and 2022-2026 (facelift) headlights are completely different and not interchangeable.
before.solution: Light fogging that clears after running the headlights a few minutes is considered normal. If you see water droplets/streaks or pooling, document it (photos over time) and pursue a warranty assembly replacement — dealers replace the full headlamp unit, which requires removing the front bumper cover. Minor recurring condensation can sometimes be managed by replacing the internal desiccant pack. Confirm you order the correct generation: pre-facelift (2019-2021) vs facelift (2022-2026) assemblies are not interchangeable.
symptoms: Visible fog, water streaks, or droplets inside the headlight lens
Water pooling at the bottom of the housing
Turn signal / DRL or low-beam intermittently not working
Complete headlight failure after prolonged moisture

proposal.solution: Inspect the moisture pattern using the bulletin criteria. Normal condensation can clear after the lamps operate with the engine running or during driving; persistent water pooling, electrical failure, physical damage, or a condition outside the bulletin criteria requires dealer diagnosis before assembly replacement.

before.title: High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure Causing Power Loss (Recall 24V-528 / 023G)
before.description: The fuel control valve inside the high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) can stick or allow excess fuel into the system, producing an air/fuel mixture that runs too rich. This causes a reduction or loss of motive power at low speeds, rough running, and check-engine warnings — increasing crash risk. Genesis recalled certain 2019-2023 G70 vehicles under NHTSA campaign 24V-528 (Genesis recall 023G); owner letters mailed September 2024. Many owners also reported the symptom (hesitation/near-stall when driving off within ~30 seconds of a cold start) before the formal recall. The remedy is an ECM software update plus inspection and replacement of the HPFP assembly as necessary, performed free of charge under the recall.
before.solution: First verify the VIN against Recall 24V-528 (023G) — the fix is free under recall. Dealers apply an updated ECM/engine-control software calibration and inspect the high-pressure fuel pump, replacing the pump assembly if it fails inspection. Out of warranty/recall, the OEM HPFP is replaced; the 3.3T uses Hyundai/Genesis pump 35320-3L000 and the 2.0T uses 35320-2CTB1. After replacement, clear codes and confirm fuel-rail pressure is within spec.
symptoms: Loss of power or hesitation accelerating from a stop or at low speed
Engine wants to stall if you drive off within ~30 seconds of starting
Rough running / engine surging
Check engine light, sometimes with a fuel-rail-pressure code
Long crank or hard start

before.title: Parasitic Battery Drain / Dead 12V Battery
before.description: G70 owners report the 12V battery going dead, sometimes overnight or after the car sits a few days, leaving the vehicle unable to start. Beyond normal battery aging, a recurring cause is parasitic draw — modules not fully going to sleep. The head unit/infotainment has been identified by owners as continuing to draw power with the car off, and other always-on modules can keep the draw above the normal sub-25 mA sleep target. The result is repeated no-starts even on cars with a healthy battery.
before.solution: Load-test the battery and check charging-system output first; replace the AGM battery if it fails. If the battery is good, measure parasitic draw with a multimeter after the modules sleep (target under ~25-50 mA) and pull fuses to isolate the offending circuit — the head unit/infotainment is a common culprit. Apply any infotainment/BMS software updates, and have the dealer check for related service campaigns. A battery maintainer helps cars that sit for long periods.
symptoms: Dead battery / no-crank after the car sits overnight or a few days
Slow engine crank, dim lights, clicking when starting
Battery repeatedly dies even after replacement
Electronics behaving oddly before a no-start

proposal.title: Extended 12-Volt Battery Diagnosis Bulletin
proposal.description: Genesis bulletin 10247603 covers 2019-2023 G70 vehicles and provides an extended GDS battery-diagnosis procedure. It evaluates internal short circuit, deterioration, electronic-component malfunction, insufficient charge, charging defects, and the preceding 30 days of state-of-charge and parasitic-draw history.
proposal.solution: Use the Genesis GDS battery diagnosis and saved battery-sensor history before replacing the battery or blaming a module. Follow the result-specific charging, electrical-system, or battery procedure; a dead battery alone does not establish parasitic draw.

before.title: Power-Folding Mirror Failure (Clicking / Not Folding or Unfolding)
before.description: As G70s age, the power-folding side mirrors develop a clicking noise and fail to fold or unfold reliably — commonly the passenger mirror not unfolding on unlock, or a mirror that won't latch into the deployed position and drifts back from wind while driving. The usual cause is worn internal plastic fold gears in the mirror actuator, though some cases are an accidentally-toggled fold setting or a loose door-harness connector.
before.solution: Rule out the easy causes first: confirm the mirror-fold switch/setting wasn't bumped off, and reseat the door-harness connector (the rectangular plug with a black locking tab inside the door frame), which has fixed some cases. If the mirror clicks and won't move, the actuator's internal fold gears are stripped — replace the fold motor/gear set or the mirror actuator assembly. Severe cases require the full mirror assembly.
symptoms: Clicking/grinding noise when mirrors try to fold or unfold
Passenger mirror doesn't unfold on unlock
Mirror won't latch out and folds back from wind while driving
One or both mirrors stop folding entirely

before.title: Soft Clear Coat — Easy Chipping, Peeling and Swirl Marks
before.description: Owners across Genesis models, including the G70, report unusually soft paint and clear coat. The clear coat scratches and swirls very easily (even careful washing can mar it), the front end picks up many rock chips in only a few thousand miles, and some cars develop clear-coat bubbling or peeling — typically at the bumper, roof rails and panel edges — exposing the base coat. It mirrors the well-documented paint complaints on the Kia Stinger. While cosmetic, it drives meaningful owner dissatisfaction and out-of-pocket repaint/PPF costs.
before.solution: For chips and stone damage, paint protection film (PPF) on the hood, fenders and mirrors is the most common preventive fix. For swirls, use proper two-bucket wash technique and a light machine polish followed by a ceramic coating to add a sacrificial layer. Document clear-coat bubbling/peeling early and pursue it under the paint warranty — some dealers have repainted affected panels for owners showing adhesion failure.
symptoms: Numerous rock chips on the front end at low mileage
Swirl marks / fine scratches appearing from normal washing
Clear coat bubbling or peeling at bumpers, roof rails or edges
Base/flat paint showing through where clear coat lifted

before.description: On the second-generation 3.5L twin-turbo G90, the retention fasteners on the fuel crossover pipe at the fuel-rail connections were tightened during assembly with an insufficient concentration of thread/torque stabilizer (thread retainer). It affects 4,231 G90 units within a larger ~94,760-vehicle Genesis action (G80/GV80/GV70 also covered), part of a combined ~235,000-unit Kia-Genesis fuel-leak action. before.solution: Under recall, dealers inspect the fuel crossover pipe and its fasteners, re-tighten them to spec with the correct torque stabilizer, and replace the fuel pipe if a leak or damage is found - free of charge regardless of warranty status, with reimbursement for prior out-of-pocket repairs. NHTSA advises parking outside and away from structures until the repair is done. VINs became searchable on NHTSA.gov April 11, 2026 and owner letters were mailed June 8, 2026.

before.title: Panoramic sunroof creaking, rattling and wind noise (loose/under-torqued frame bolts)
before.description: First-generation (DH) G90 sedans with the large panoramic glass roof commonly develop creaks, rattles and squeaks from the roof/headliner area, plus wind-noise vibration over the glass. Root causes owners and dealers have found include sunroof frame/track attachment bolts that back off or were under-torqued from the factory (one documented case found 32 loose bolts), plus metal-on-metal contact in the frame. Genesis addresses the noise complaints with TSB 23-BD-014G. Note: some owners also report spontaneous panoramic-glass shattering (a known Hyundai/Kia glass-roof failure mode), but that is less well documented specifically on the G90 and coverage is often disputed absent proven breakage.
before.solution: Per TSB 23-BD-014G, install the sunroof felt/anti-noise kit (adds felt padding and lubricant to stop metal-on-metal movement) and fit modified sunroof frame bolts torqued to spec; loose factory bolts are re-torqued. In stubborn cases the roof/sunroof frame assembly is replaced. For a shattered glass panel, the sunroof glass or full assembly is replaced.
symptoms: Creaking/squeaking from the roof or headliner over bumps
Rattling or buzzing from the sunroof glass area
Excessive wind noise or vibration at highway speed
Loud bang and glass falling into cabin (spontaneous glass shatter, less common)

before.title: Power trunk fails to close/latch or release, often due to lid misalignment
before.description: Owners of the power-operated trunk on the first-generation G90 report intermittent failures where the decklid will not fully close and latch when lowered, or will not release and rise when commanded (some report a stick roughly every few openings). The trunk uses a power latch (cinch) module and a power drive (raise/lower) module, either of which can fail or fall out of calibration. Owner and dealer reports indicate lid misalignment is a frequent root cause - striker, rubber stopper and trim adjustment often resolves it - and that simply replacing the latch and drive motor does not always help. Low 12V battery voltage can also cause the symptom. This is a body/closure electromechanical issue distinct from the general parasitic battery-drain complaint.
before.solution: Dealers typically start by adjusting the striker, bump stops/rubber stoppers and plastic trim to correct alignment, and check the release switch/harness and battery voltage; a full re-charge sometimes restores operation. Where the actuators are actually failed, the power latch assembly and/or power drive unit are replaced and the trunk initialization/re-learn is run. Under warranty the repair is free; out of warranty, actuator/latch parts plus labor typically run several hundred to over a thousand dollars.
symptoms: Trunk does not fully close/cinch when lowered
Trunk fails to open or release when the button/fob is pressed
Intermittent, hard-to-reproduce operation (e.g., every few tries)
Trunk-ajar warning despite the lid appearing shut

before.description: Owners across model years report the 12V battery going flat after the car sits a few days. before.description: Owners across both the ICE and Electrified GV70 report the 12V battery going dead after the car sits for only a few days, leaving the vehicle unresponsive and unable to start ('bricked'). On Electrified GV70s, confirm the ICCU recalls (025G / 24V-204 family) are completed, since ICCU failure is a major cause of repeat 12V deaths. Persistent draw with no obvious cause warrants module-by-module isolation by the dealer.

before.description: Gasoline GV70 owners (2.5T and 3.5T) report a throttle-tip-in delay followed by an abrupt jolt, plus hard or jerky downshifts from the 8-speed automatic (Hyundai A8LR1/A8TR1), most noticeable accelerating out of a turn or in Sport mode. In hardware cases, dealers have replaced the throttle body (and, for some, fuel injectors), which resolved the hesitation; a minority of intermittent cases traced to coolant leaks putting the car in limp mode were fixed by hose/radiator repair.

Driver-side vents warm while passenger side is cold (or vice versa)

before.title: Headlight Assembly Moisture and Condensation Buildup
before.description: A frequently cited exterior/lighting complaint on the GV70 is moisture and condensation forming inside the LED headlight housings, ranging from light fogging after a car wash to visible water pooling at the bottom of the assembly. Owners report the condensation blurs the LED beam pattern, reduces nighttime illumination, and raises the risk of premature LED failure from repeated water-vapor exposure. before.title: ICCU Failure Causing Loss of Drive Power (Electrified GV70)
before.description: The Integrated Charging Control Unit (ICCU) manages charging of the high-voltage pack and the 12V battery that runs accessories and control modules. The ICCU (and its internal fuse) can become damaged and stop charging the 12V system. The car then enters a fail-safe mode with warning lights, audible alerts, and reduced power; if driving continues it can fully lose drive power, sometimes preceded by an audible 'pop.' Drivers typically have ~22-45 minutes to pull over, with steering and brakes still functional. Genesis covered this under recalls tied to NHTSA 24V-204, expanded/replaced by Genesis 025G (Dec 2024), part of the broad Hyundai/Kia/Genesis ICCU campaign. The failed ICCU also produces dead-12V 'bricked' no-start events.
before.solution: Verify the VIN against the ICCU recalls (Genesis 025G; NHTSA 24V-204 and its expansions). Dealers inspect and replace the ICCU and its fuse as necessary and apply updated ICCU software, free of charge. If you experience warning lights plus a power-reduction message, pull over and arrange transport rather than continuing to drive. A repeat dead-12V battery on an Electrified GV70 should trigger an ICCU diagnosis, not just a battery swap.
symptoms: Loss of drive power / reduced propulsion while driving
Audible 'pop' then warning lights and alarms
Repeated dead 12V battery / no-start ('bricked')
Vehicle fails to DC fast charge or AC charge
Check electric vehicle system warning

before.title: Instrument Cluster Blank or Flickering at Startup
before.description: Incorrect software logic in the screen-initialization protocol (memory loading and error storage) can cause the digital instrument panel cluster to flicker or go completely blank at startup. Owners noticing stalling, hesitation, or hard starts in hot weather should have the recall completed before further driving.

before.title: Rear Differential / eLSD Whine and Repeat Carrier Failure
before.description: AWD GV70s (both 2.5T and 3.5T) develop a whining, humming, or droning noise from the rear axle, often at highway speed and frequently before the break-in period is even over. The condition is tied to the rear differential carrier and, on Sport/3.5T trims, the electronic limited-slip differential (eLSD). Genesis acknowledged it with TSB 23-DS-004G / 23-DS-004G-1, which walks dealers through noise inspection, lock-nut re-torque, re-inspection, and full carrier replacement. The biggest owner frustration is repeat failure: dealers swap in the same-design carrier and the replacement units whine again within thousands of miles, with one 3.5T owner reporting a second failure at ~3,700 miles after a new carrier and another reporting two eLSD replacements under 8,000 miles.
before.solution: Have the dealer perform TSB 23-DS-004G/-1: inspect and re-torque the differential carrier lock nut, road-test, and if noise persists replace the rear differential carrier assembly (and the eLSD-equipped carrier on Sport/3.5T) under the 5yr/60k powertrain warranty, followed by a rear-axle alignment. Because the same-design part can fail again, document each occurrence in writing for lemon-law leverage and ask whether an updated revision carrier is available before authorizing a like-for-like swap.
symptoms: Whining or humming from the rear of the vehicle
Droning noise that rises with road speed
Noise present from very low mileage
Recurrence of noise shortly after a differential replacement
